open.title: THE BLUEPRINT + LIVE RE-SOLVE ARCHITECTURE — WILL, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenar
open.full: the blueprint + live re-solve architecture — will, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenario that people try and memorize, i want that for us, so we can try searching for the most similar scenario from a repository as well as live rollout"*, alongside *"i dont want to behavior clone first i want to try our searching and poker like simulation"*. this is the architecture that beat humans at nlhe — libratus and pluribus do not play off charts, they compute a coarse blueprint offline and do real-time subgame re-solving at the table. blueprint + live search is exactly what he described, and it is a far better fit here than behaviour cloning: vgc-bench trains offline so inference is cheap, whereas search pays per turn on a clock. the endgame half is already scoped and small — #47 measures 1v1 at 16 cells, 2v1 at 96, 2v2 at ~1,296, with 2v1 alone reachable in 45.9% of games; retrograde analysis builds up from there (#30, #40, #41). the early game is the research problem and it is the abstraction, not the retrieval. poker charts work on isomorphism — a(s)k(s) and a(h)k(h) are one hand — and pokemon has no isomorphism that clean, because which species is on the field is the information content. so the repository needs a learned similarity metric. we have a candidate and it has been tested in the wrong direction: #23 gated porygon2 on whether it can separate positions two turns apart; retrieval needs the inverse, that genuinely similar positions land close. same encoder, opposite test, never run. the honest dependency: the re-solve half needs a fast simulator, which loops back to #62 and to the poke-env benchmark nobody has ever taken

open.title: THE END GOAL, STATED SO PRIORITIES CAN BE ARGUED AGAINST IT — WILL, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sh
open.full: the end goal, stated so priorities can be argued against it — will, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sheets and get to number 1 on the ladder but we are far off"*. it had never been written down, so every ordering argument in this register was being made against a target nobody had stated. it is a curriculum, not a mismatch — will corrected this the same day: *"once we solve open team sheets, we can think about the more difficult closed team sheets and adapt our models accordingly"*. i first filed the open-sheet corpus against a closed-sheet target as a violation of this file's *fitting environment must match playing environment* rule. that was an over-application. the rule governs fitting and playing in the same deployment; deliberately solving the fully-observable version first and adapting afterwards is staging, and staging is how you get a measurable baseline at all. what survives is narrower and still worth holding: a model fitted where every set is known must be able to accept uncertainty about sets later, and that is an architecture question better answered before everything is built assuming certainty — the same lesson as the focus sash drag, where replacing a hedge with a certainty inherited responsibility for every event that staled it. and it flips the poker argument the right way. open sheets strip out most hidden information and make our game easier than poker in the dimension poker is hardest; closed sheets put it back — unknown items, spreads, the fourth move, which four of six they brought — so information sets become the game and #163's blueprint+re-solve becomes the right primitive rather than a flourish. two things already built for other reasons are the closed-sheet machinery: #52 hypno (rate the opponent, decide how hard to exploit — deferred by will) and the prefer observed over declared rule with its knock off / trick / consumed-berry tracking, which is exactly the inference a closed-sheet bot needs. will's own farigiraf/cud chew read is the same idea from the player side: a bluff that exists only because sheets are closed, and that open sheets delete. "far off" is accurate — #62 unanswered, ~26 open rows in the medicham block, no search redesign started

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: ARGMAX IS UNSOUND IN A SIMULTANEOUS-MOVE GAME, AND OPEN TEAM SHEETS DO NOT RESCUE IT — CITED, 2026-08-11. Bosansky, Lisy
open.full: argmax is unsound in a simultaneous-move game, and open team sheets do not rescue it — cited, 2026-08-11. bosansky, lisy, lanctot, cermak & winands, *algorithms for computing strategies in two-player simultaneous move games*, artificial intelligence 237 (2016) 1-40: agents *"may need to use randomized (or mixed) strategies in order to play optimally ... even though the only information that is hidden is each player's action as they play it"*. simultaneity alone forces mixing. i had told will the opposite — that open sheets make our game easier than poker in poker's hardest dimension. on this axis they do not. what medicham is: `miltank.js:1315` is `if (v > bestval) { bestval = v; bestpair = [ia, ib]; }` and `:1384` clicks it — a plain argmax, deterministic by construction, answerable for free by anyone who knows the scorer. magnemite underneath it does sample (`magnemite.js:954`, `:1154`, a softmax its own header calls *"the single biggest measured lever"* and which argues *"taking the argmax would be the obvious thing and it is wrong here"*), so the bot gets less mixed as it gets smarter — the 31.6% of turns miltank defers are the only ones that come out mixed, which inverts #62: more compute means fewer deferrals means more predictable. duct is not the fix — i had it in the fix list and the paper reports it *"also might not converge to a nash equilibrium"*, even the mixed variant; uct's failure is shown on biased rock-paper-scissors (shafiei, sturtevant & schaeffer, giga 2009). what is sound, three tiers from that paper: exact backward induction solving the matrix game per node, which *"outputs a subgame perfect ne"*; sm-oos, which *"guarantee[s] to closely approximate the optimal strategies given enough time"*; and sm-mcts-rm (regret matching at simultaneous nodes) as the practical middle. so roadmap #41's python equilibrium solver is the textbook-correct primitive for this game class, currently filed as *"the equilibrium answer exists and cannot play"*. and unlike pluribus we are 1v1 zero-sum, so the *"equilibrium is not the right goal"* retreat does not apply to us — equilibrium is the target here. phase 3, not now: medicham is phase 1 and a correct simulator is a prerequisite under every version of this. registered so it is not rediscovered

open.full: the rate runner must play the staged scenarios, not random self-play — will's design, 2026-08-11. will: *"the million game run will be all these staging scenarios right, just with normal accuracy, proc chances, crit chances, etc"*, then *"so those will have to be in the million game run"*. one set of fixtures at two dice settings: the roster plays a staged board with the dice pinned and asks *does it do the right thing when it fires*; 78,494 / 21 s for 2 points; 19,758 / 6 s for 5. a staged battle is one constructed four-body board played for one turn at 0.26 ms — not comparable to a self-play game, which is why 'a million games' was always the wrong unit. the rule earned itself immediately: at 2 points effect spore read 31.90% and diverged at 95%, with a split-half spread of 1.97 against an effect of 1.90 — not an effect (lessons §9) — and at the powered n it reads 30.34%. a row stopped early is not a smaller answer, it is a different one. and the instrument's own three bugs were found before publication: the first version matched the tag's status word against the engine's and read flame body 0/40 and poison point 0/40 — a headline that would have been filed against engine — because the tag speaks `burn`/`poison`/`sleep` and the engine speaks `brn`/`psn`/`slp`, and static passed by pure accident on three shared letters; open.full: the whole-game differential says 39.6% of games diverge, it gates nothing, and i quoted the damage number all session as if it covered this , closed 2026-08-12. `engine/game_differential.js` plays one team pair through both engines with real sheets and real natures, pins every die identically on both sides so any difference is a rule bug, and records the first divergence. re-run on release 5a557b07821c: 1,213 games, 480 diverged (39.6%), 0 threw, planted proof caught. the previous run was 570 of 1,556 (36.6%) — a full evening of engine work did not move it, which is itself the finding. the gate's `game differential` clause reads `data/engine-diff.json`, which is damage only and says 0 of 6,000 — its own scope line reads *'no items or abilities. turn order, status duration and switching need a different harness and are not attempted here rather than attempted badly.'* both numbers are true; they answer different questions; i conflated them in the project's favour repeatedly and will caught it by asking whether we had ever played the same game on both engines. new `engine/divergence_report.js` rolls the causes up — the artifact has recorded every one since it was built and nothing had ever read them. 307 distinct causes, 251 appearing in exactly one game. ranked by corpus usage rather than by count, because the swarm is coverage-steered so its game counts describe the instrument while the corpus counts describe what people click. the two rankings disagree and both are needed: by games the head is residual weather order, ~80 games — six causes identical in shape, differing only in which body is chipped first, one rule; by usage the head is protect, 32 games but 94,313 clicks, where showdown says the move worked and we say it failed, scattered across four of the differential's classes at once, which is why the class view hid it re-measured 2026-08-18 by measure, and the gating half finally has a command. the gate landed 2026-08-12 as clause 7 of 7 of a four-minute report, which is not a thing `engine/register_reality.js` can run — so this row still had no instrument, and #297's closed-detector repair reopened it. `node engine/quarantine.js --whole-game` is that same clause with a process exit attached and nothing else: it calls `wholegameclause` rather than restating it, and both it and `--order-probe` map their verdict through one `clauseexit`, so a withheld figure cannot exit 0 through one command and 2 through the other. 0 = the two engines agree on every game, 1 = they do not, 2 = the artifact describes other bytes (#298). measured on a differential re-run of the current tree — 995 games, arm a/middle, release `978ca8fe72c9`, census `2e3953f1f882`, team pool `631d4ea60a80` — it is 696 of 995 = 69.9% (700 raw, less 4 declared, 0 cleared on decision impact) and it exits 1. the 39.6% in this title and the 33.4% in this cell are not a trend with it. different releases, different pins and different samples: the driver steers off a census that is regenerated and picks pairs from a team pool read live from the store, so two runs a day apart do not play the same games. verified by: `node engine/quarantine.js --whole-game`

open.title: A DATA-ONLY COMMIT CAN ORPHAN EVERY FIGURE IN A LIVING DOC, AND THE HOOK THAT WATCHES FOR THAT SKIPS DATA-ONLY COMMITS —
open.full: a data-only commit can orphan every figure in a living doc, and the hook that watches for that skips data-only commits — 2026-08-11. `tests/test-docs-current.js` calls a figure traceable when some artifact contains it. `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md` recorded the first rate run — 16,575 trials, 30.42%, the confidence intervals — and every one was traceable because `data/million-run.json` held it. re-running the same instrument overwrote the artifact with new numbers and orphaned nineteen figures at a stroke. nothing was typed and nothing became false; the doc still describes what was measured, and the artifact that proved it no longer exists. isolated rather than assumed: at head with none of the evening's doc edits applied the count already read 47 against a baseline of 28, so only one of the twenty came from the pass being committed. the reason it went unseen is the hole: `.githooks/pre-commit` skips data-only commits, so the run that rewrote the artifact was exactly the commit the gate did not inspect. baseline raised 28 -> 48 with the diff shown (two lines, the count and the timestamp, nothing else laundered). the structural weakness is real and is not fixed by this row: the check cannot tell 'a figure nobody measured' from 'a figure whose instrument has since been re-run', and it will fire again on every re-run. the candidate repair is to make a re-run stamp the figures it supersedes — a doc figure would then cite a run rather than a value, which is the same lesson as the frozen release and is a bigger job than a baseline bump. recorded now because the alternative is that the next person raises the number again and the ratchet quietly becomes decoration

the weather loop one screen above kept iterating `[...acta, ...actb]`. nothing could have caught it: every body takes the same 1/16, so every total agreed and a damage differential is structurally blind to an ordering defect. fixed as one `residualorder(acta, actb, field)` that both passes ask, with #115's three inline lines deleted rather than left beside it — re-sorting the weather loop in place would have written the fact twice with the same chance of drifting apart again. probe `move/weathersetter`, four bodies at speed 205/101/80, and the trick room arm is the discriminator: `getactionspeed` returns `10000 - speed`, so the inversion is already inside the number both passes sort on and no second branch exists — an engine sorting by raw speed passes arm 1 and fails arm 2, slot order fails both. garchomp on the board takes no chip, the control that says this is the sand. verified independently of the agent's report: the both-sides family reads 3 causes / 4 games against 6 / 80 | reopened 2026-08-12 — the explanation was wrong and the 32 games are unexplained again. this row said protect's divergences were an instrument artefact: our stall counter shares the scalar die, so mode a's corner forces every consecutive protect to fail. the coupling is real and the first protect is clean under both pins — but that cannot be the cause, because showdown's stall check is pinned to refuse at the same corner (#222, measured). both engines refuse; they were agreeing for that reason. so a trace showing the authority emit `-singleturn|protect` where we emit `-fail` is not a disagreement about the roll — it is a disagreement about the counter's value, theirs short-circuiting at `_ctr <= 1` while ours is at 2 or more. that is a rule about when the stall counter resets, which is exactly what mode a exists to find. 32 games, 94,313 corpus clicks, the most-played move in the format. recorded as reopened rather than quietly re-scoped, because the tidier story is the one that got believed twice

every stored sheet reads `evs: null`, 173,784 of 173,784 bodies. neither the blank spread nor the speed ties cause a single divergence — both are applied identically to both engines — they hide errors instead, and the file already said so in a comment nobody had acted on: *"with every body flat and serious, 91.4% of legal species share a base speed with some other species, so the rig manufactured speed ties"*. the prediction is recorded before the fact: adding spreads should make the number worse and `ordering` should grow; an unmoved rate is the suspicious outcome. second unfrozen input named the same day: the team pool is read live from stores ops appends to continuously, which is why three runs of one instrument reported 1,556, 1,213 and 983 — a measurement that freezes the engine and pins every die took its sample from a moving file. frozen on will's instruction to `data/team-pool-frozen` (bo3 13,214 lines sha 5e10d7ba991f, ots 4,167 lines sha cd21077a4578) and the first pinned baseline is 327/983 (33.3%) top-tie-first and 377/983 (38.4%) bottom-tie-first — the first whole-game figure in this project whose counts are comparable run to run. that five-point arm gap also weakens a claim i made to will off the unpinned run — i said the two corners agreed to within half a point and therefore the divergences were rules rather than dice; open.title: SOME MECHANICS ARE HARDCODED EXCEPTIONS IN THE SIMULATOR, NOT HANDLERS, AND EVERY DERIVATION BUILT TODAY IS BLIND TO THE
open.full: some mechanics are hardcoded exceptions in the simulator, not handlers, and every derivation built today is blind to them — will, 2026-08-13. he asked whether the ability that poisons steel types is even in the regulation. it is: corrosion, legal, carriers salazzle and glimmora, 36 corpus uses — and it has zero `on*` handlers. it is not an ability hook at all. it is a name written into the immunity check itself, `pokemon.js:1257`: `!(source?.hasability("corrosion") && ["tox","psn"].includes(status.id))`. this is a class, not a curiosity. ten abilities are named directly in `dist/sim/*.js` rather than reached through a handler — sheerforce, klutz, prankster, multitype, megasol, levitate, guts, eelevate, dancer, corrosion — and three carry no handlers whatever. levitate is the expensive one: 3,186 corpus uses and 0 handlers. every derivation this project built on 2026-08-12 reads handlers — the per-ability trigger derivation (`pre.moveneeds`), the preflight trigger clauses, the accmod conformance sweep, the residual-order table. all of them are structurally blind to this shape, so the abilities arm cannot stage levitate or corrosion from a handler read, and a sweep that reports "no handler, nothing to check" is reporting its own blind spot as a clean bill. `data/tags.json` does carry rows for both, so `tag_dex` reached them by another route — but that is a second derivation happening to cover the gap, not coverage by design, and nothing checks that the two agree about which abilities exist. the concrete cost, measured the same night: a diverging game showed toxic into a steel scizor — the authority emits `-immune`, we emit `-miss`, because our poison immunity check runs after the accuracy roll instead of before it. fixing that as an absolute immunity would have been wrong in the opposite direction, since a salazzle toxic into a steel body lands. will caught that before it shipped. the ordering fix and the corrosion exemption went to the agent already in `hitchance`; the general sweep — which mechanics in this format are hardcoded exceptions, and does anything verify our tags cover them — is not started

open.full: mag becomes a futility gate and stops being a learned scorer — will, 2026-08-13. *"im thinking of cutting mag back in size to say, no fake out after turn 1, no poison on steel, no status moves into gholdengo, no prio moves when farig is on the board... just very simple rules and not the whole convoluted, protect and let my partner ko the threat."* this fixes an ordering fault and is not merely a simplification. a learned mag prunes what is bad on average and runs before doduo, so it deletes precisely the actions that are bad alone and good in combination — fake out into a spread, follow me covering a setup turn, a weak click that baits a protect — which is the entire class doduo exists to find. the safe line is futile (no other action rescues it) versus bad (conditional, must survive to doduo). the gate must be derived, not written, and all four example rules are wrong as typed: fake out is `activemoveactions > 1` — first turn out, not turn 1 of the game, so a fake out user switching in on turn 6 may still use it; open.full: the word "endgame" is claimed by two models in our own ledger, and that is why the architecture was hard to hold — will, 2026-08-13. *"wait didnt we have dusknoir as the endgame guy? its hard to keep track."* he is right and the confusion is ours, not his memory. `docs/models.md:1451` scopes dusk as the endgame tablebase — exact, precomputed offline, shipped as a lookup because it cannot be solved under a turn timer. slowking's job: line in the same file reads *"the endgame — tell you the equilibrium-best move (and win %) on a live position"*, which is not distinguishable in wording. the split, now written down: dusk is small endgames, exact, offline then looked up; slowking is any position, approximate (an equilibrium over estimated values), live per turn; hypno is about the opponent rather than the position and is a deliberate deviation from slowking. only dusk can say "guaranteed" — which means will's own description of the late-game stage (*"which ones lead to a guaranteed win... hand these scenarios to miltank"*) is dusk's job and was filed under hypno. fixed in `docs/models.md` and `docs/alakazam-v2-spec.md`. and the matrix is kept even if greedy wins: *"id still want slowking matrix even if greedy wins right? because then if we play opponents regularly we can adapt and become unexploitable."* keeping it is right and is already adr-003's position — vgc-bench's policy beats a worlds competitor and is ~100% exploitable, so winning on average and being safe are different axes. one correction to the reasoning: adapting to an opponent makes you more exploitable, not less. nash never adapts and cannot be beaten in the long run; deviating to punish a habit opens a hole in you. what repeated play actually buys is the other direction — a fixed policy degrades because they learn you, and greedy is a fixed mapping. the matrix is not the adaptation mechanism; it is the floor you measure your deviations against, and hypno is the deviation

open.title: "EVERY SECONDARY FIRES" SELF-CANCELS FOR ANY EFFECT WITH AN ESCAPE ROLL, SO THE BOTTOM ARM GUARANTEES FREEZE AND GUARANT
open.full: "every secondary fires" self-cancels for any effect with an escape roll, so the bottom arm guarantees freeze and guarantees thaw — will, 2026-08-13. *"bro guaranteed freeze in the lower bound is so broken"*, then, one message later, *"but i guess we get guaranteed thaw?"* — both right, and together they name a property of the instrument nobody had stated. `makearm` pins `random(den)` to 0 in the bottom arm, and `chance = (num, den) => random(den) < num`, so every `randomchance` returns true. the freeze secondary (`randomchance(1,10)`) fires and the thaw check inside `frz.onbeforemove` (`randomchance(1,4)`) also fires, so a body is frozen and cures on its very next move without ever losing a turn. the bottom arm therefore never exercises frozen-turn behaviour at all, while appearing to guarantee it. the effect is not uniform and that is the point: an effect with one roll compounds (paralysis is applied and fully paralyses every turn; confusion is applied and self-hits), an effect with an escape roll cancels (freeze). *"the worst corner"* is therefore the wrong mental model for this arm — it is *"every branch taken"*, which is the worst case only when there is one branch. not a defect in the pin, which is doing exactly what it says; it is a coverage claim that needs narrowing, and the arm's own description (*"every secondary fires"*) is what misleads. and a latent collision found while checking it: `random(m)` returns the damage index when `m === damage_roll_sides` (16), so any `randomchance(x, 16)` would be read as a damage roll rather than a chance. derived: no legal move in this regulation has a 1-in-16 secondary, so it is latent today and would surface silently the day one is added

open.title: A MIDDLE ARM WITH EVENT-ADDRESSED DICE, BECAUSE BOTH PINNED CORNERS PRODUCE GAMES NOBODY PLAYS — WILL, 2026-08-13. *"is
open.full: a middle arm with event-addressed dice, because both pinned corners produce games nobody plays — will, 2026-08-13. *"is it possible at all for us to run a middle bound? where things can miss, and secondary chances have a chance to proc? to get some more realistic scenarios to test... otherwise paralysis ends the mons usefulness... thats why games take years."* he is right about the mechanism and it is measurable: the bottom arm pins every `randomchance` true (see #260), so the full-paralysis roll fires every turn and a paralysed body never moves again — which is a large part of why the median game hits the 12-turn cap when a real one ends at 7. why random dice are not the answer, and this is the whole design problem: the arms are pinned for synchronisation, not caution. both engines must give the same answer to the same question or a divergence is a dice disagreement rather than a rule disagreement, and they make different numbers of draws in different orders, so a shared seeded stream desynchronises on turn one. a constant is the only mapping that survives that. the way out is to address the die by the event rather than by position in a sequence: `hash(turn, attacker slot, move id, effect name) % 100 < chance`. order-independent, so the engines agree without being in lockstep; some rock slides miss and some flinch; paralysis fires near 1-in-4 instead of every turn; games end. across thousands of events the observed rates approach the printed ones, which also makes it the natural home for the rate work in #196/#28. the cost, stated: the two engines must name the event identically — same move id, same turn, same target — or the hashes differ and every roll disagrees. the normaliser already maps ids, so it is checkable, and it must be asserted rather than assumed: a probe that plants a known event on both sides and compares the drawn value. and it inherits #260: an effect with an escape roll must not get "true" for both the apply and the escape, which a hash gives for free and a constant never can | engine half landed 2026-08-13 — the engine names the event; open.title: THE STORE HAS NO SPREADS AT ALL, SO A REPLAY DIFFERENTIAL CANNOT ADJUDICATE DAMAGE OR SPEED — WILL, 2026-08-13, AND HE T
open.full: the store has no spreads at all, so a replay differential cannot adjudicate damage or speed — will, 2026-08-13, and he talked me out of leading with it. i proposed running `engine/replay_differential.js` against real games as the realistic instrument. *"we dont know the sps on games that actually happened tho"*, then *"so the damage and speed would be off."* measured on `data/games.bo3.jsonl`: 4,001 games, 47,856 sheet bodies, every one `"evs": null`, zero with a real spread. an open team sheet shows species, ability, item, moves and nature — never the stat points. speed is the worse half and that is the part i missed: damage being off produces a wrong number, but speed being off produces a wrong turn order, which is categorical — every line after it diverges for a reason that is not a rule. `replay_differential.js`'s own header already makes this argument about reconstructing choices (*"a reconstruction that guesses is worse than no test, because a guess that happens to be wrong looks exactly like an engine defect"*) and does not apply it to the spreads. the distinction that matters is control, not realism: the synthetic differential's spreads are unknown and identical on both sides, so a divergence can only be a rule; a replay's spreads are unknown and different from whatever the player actually brought, so a divergence may be either. unknown-but-identical is fine; unknown-and-wrong is not. so the replay differential keeps a narrower job — sequences and categorical facts independent of exact numbers (did that ability fire, did that switch happen, was that move legal) — and cannot arbitrate a ko or a speed tie, which is most of what a game turns on. this is roadmap #68 restated with its consequence: it is narrowed by the nature and can never be closed by it. do not lead with replay; build #262 instead, which is synthetic and therefore controls its own spreads

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE WHOLE-GAME HEADLINE IS COMPUTED OVER A DENOMINATOR THAT INCLUDES 350 VOID GAMES, AND THE ARTIFACT DOES NOT CARRY THE
open.full: the whole-game headline is computed over a denominator that includes 350 void games, and the artifact does not carry the number that would fix it — found 2026-08-18 by measure while re-running the differential. `engine/game_differential.js` declares its own rule in the middle arm's description: *a game whose draw counts diverge is void, not a divergence*. its stdout reports all three figures — `diverged (primary arm middle): 700 of 995`, `void (instrument desync): 350 of 995`, `diverged among the 645 usable games: 628 (97.4%)` — and the artifact persists only `games: 995` and `diverged: 700`. so `wholegameclause` publishes 700 (less declared) over 995, and by the run's own arithmetic 72 of those 700 diverged games are themselves void: 700 — 628 = 72, and 995 — 350 = 645. the honest figure is worse, not better. on the games where the instrument is valid the engines disagree about 628 of 645 = 97.4%, where the clause's own ratio is 69.9%. neither number can be published by the clause today, because the void count exists only in a console line nobody parses. this is not a request to change the bar: the clause is green only at zero either way. it is that the most-quoted number in this project is a ratio of two quantities that do not describe the same population, and a reader cannot tell from the artifact. measured on release `978ca8fe72c9`, 995 games, arm a/middle, census `2e3953f1f882`, pool `631d4ea60a80`; the identical split appears on release `6875c8ace00e` under the same steering. instrument owed: the artifact must persist `void` and `usable` beside `games` and `diverged`, and then `wholegameclause` must publish the usable rate — a clause cannot derive a denominator that was never written down. landed 2026-08-18 by engine, and the population was not what the void rule said it was. `mid_void` is now in the artifact — `void_games`, `usable_games`, `diverged_among_usable`, `diverged_rate_over_usable`, and every verdict the check reached by cause. printing the causes killed the headline: 340 of 350 voided games had drawn no comparable address at all, 275 of them because neither engine rolled a die in the whole game (median 12 turns, the cap). under the count-based check an empty side meant the streams had parted; under shared-address identity there is nothing to disagree about, and the rule already said so two clauses down for the outcome log while contradicting itself for the full one. a dice-free game is the most trustworthy evidence in the run, not the least. and the real desync was #302, one file over. void on the same 797-game sample: 350 (old rule) -> 11 (rule corrected) -> 8 (#302 fixed). verified by tests/test-middle-draw-scope.js, whose §6 re-runs itself with `--mid-carry-nth` and fails if the broken arm passes

open.title: THE CATCH BLOCK THAT REPORTS A FAILED SHOWDOWN WRAP CANNOT RUN, SO A BAD `SHOWDOWN_PATH` KILLS THE DIFFERENTIAL WITH A T
open.full: the catch block that reports a failed showdown wrap cannot run, so a bad `showdown_path` kills the differential with a temporal-dead-zone error naming neither cause nor cure — found 2026-08-18 by measure, by walking into it. `engine/game_differential.js:244` assigns `mid_wrap_error = e.message` inside the catch that guards the middle-arm wrapper; `mid_wrap_error` is declared `let` at :743, five hundred lines below. the assignment is therefore in the variable's temporal dead zone and throws. reproduced: a `showdown_path` carrying one trailing space (`set var=x && ...` in cmd keeps it) makes the `require` fail, and the process dies with `referenceerror: cannot access 'mid_wrap_error' before initialization` at line 244 — which names the reporting variable and says nothing about the path, the require, or the wrapper. the error path is the part that does not work, which is this repository's founding shape pointed the other way: not a capability absent and everything reporting success, but a capability whose failure report is the thing that is broken. it is latent while the wrap succeeds, so no run that worked has ever touched it, and `mid_wrap_error === null` is asserted by a pin claim that can never see this branch. cost measured at one wasted run and about ten minutes of looking for an engine bug that was a shell quoting mistake. the repair is to hoist the declaration above the try. instrument owed: an arm that loads the driver with a deliberately wrong `showdown_path` and asserts the process reports the require failure rather than a `referenceerror`

open.full: `switch lookups that missed: medicham 22, showdown 0` on a line the run itself marks `must read 0`, and nothing gates it — found 2026-08-18 by measure. the whole-game differential prints this counter with its own bar attached and its own consequence spelled out beside it: *a miss means that side passed while the other switched*. so on those lookups the two engines are not playing the same game at all — one body left the field and the other did not — and every line after it is compared across two different positions. measured: 22 misses on the medicham side and 0 on the authority's, on release `978ca8fe72c9` over 995 games, and the identical 22/0 on release `6875c8ace00e` under the same steering, so it is not a regression from either of today's landings. it is reported here rather than repaired because `engine/game_differential.js` and the simulator are engine's and were live while this ran. the counter is not persisted in the artifact either, so nothing downstream can read it. instrument owed: the miss count published in the artifact and a clause that fails while it is non-zero, since a run marked must read 0 that reads 22 is currently caught only by a human reading stdout

open.title: THE AUTHORITY'S REPEAT INDEX SURVIVED THE GAME BOUNDARY, SO THE TWO ENGINES DREW DIFFERENT VALUES FOR THE SAME EVENT IN
open.full: the authority's repeat index survived the game boundary, so the two engines drew different values for the same event in every measured game — found and fixed 2026-08-18 by engine. the middle arm's die is `fnv1a(seed|turn|category|move|target|nth)`, and `nth` — the repeat index — is a field of the hash. medicham2 clears its map once per game inside `mideventdice`. the driver's `mid_nth` and its authority address log were cleared by the void check instead, which runs once per pair — after both the stones-removed control game and the measured one. so every address the control game touched was left at nth=1,2,3..., the measured game's authority draws continued from there, and medicham2 started at 0. 846 of 878 unshared addresses in a 260-game run differed in `nth` and in nothing else. the log half made the check too lenient rather than too harsh, which is why nothing noticed: `shared` is `meo.filter(a => sdset.has(a))`, so an address the authority only asked in the control game counted as agreement — measured on game one as `sd=1075 me=11`. same shape as #220 and larger: #220 mis-addressed the draws made outside three `battleactions` methods, this mis-addressed every authority draw in every game that had a control in front of it. fix is the reset moved to the top of `playgame`, beside `arm.medirng()`, which is the one place that already knows a game is starting. paired on 797 games, release `978ca8fe72c9`, census and pool pinned, the driver the only file that moved: diverged 487 -> 452, void 11 -> 8, games positively verified as naming the same events 208 -> 231. verified by tests/test-middle-draw-scope.js — the same staged game played twice must produce the same addresses and the same trace; `--mid-carry-nth` restores the leak and the file fails if that arm does not go red

open.title: THE LARGEST CLASS IN THE WHOLE-GAME DIFFERENTIAL WAS A SHARED DIE READ BACKWARDS ON ONE SIDE — FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-1
open.full: the largest class in the whole-game differential was a shared die read backwards on one side — found and fixed 2026-08-18 by engine. `-damage field 3` was 226 of 491 diverging games while `tests/test-engine-diff.js` reads 0 of 6000 at each corner and `game_differential.js`'s own header says *"the engines agree about damage"*. both were true: the corner is exactly where the defect cannot show. showdown's `random(16)` is an index and `randomizer` is `tr(tr(d*(100-i))/100)`, so i=0 is the maximum; medicham2 draws a position in its span, `d.min + floor(u*(d.max-d.min+1))`, increasing in u. the pinned arms already encode the correspondence — `corner_top` sits beside `damageindex: 0`, `corner_bottom` beside `damageindex: 15` — and the middle arm handed showdown `floor(u*16)`, the inverse. a shared die read backwards on one side is anti-correlated, which is worse than two independent dice. arm split, one 969-game run, complete populations: 226 in `middle`, 2 of 155 in `top-tie-first`, 0 of 183 in `bottom-tie-first`; sampled hp deltas both signs to +/-18, median 5 — the span, not a rounding step. fix narrowed to `mid_cat === 'dmg' && m === damage_roll_sides` because `random(16)` elsewhere is a 1-in-16 chance (#260). paired on 797 games, the mapping the only thing that moved: `-damage field 3` 204 -> 137, diverged 452 -> 409, void 8 -> 4. two thirds of the family survives and is not explained — the standing candidate is a real medicham2 defect, `damage_interior`: 20 producible hp values against the authority's 14 on one staged hit, 6 of them the authority can never emit. verified by tests/test-middle-damage-roll.js, which derives the mapping from the pinned arms' own declarations and re-runs itself with `--mid-damage-uninverted`

open.title: medicham2's DAMAGE ROLL IS A UNIFORM DRAW OVER THE INTEGER SPAN; SHOWDOWN'S IS ONE OF SIXTEEN FLOORED INDICES — FOUND 20
open.full: medicham2's damage roll is a uniform draw over the integer span; showdown's is one of sixteen floored indices — found 2026-08-18 by engine, not fixed. showdown computes `tr(tr(d*(100-i))/100)` for i in 0..15, so its support has holes and repeats; medicham2 computes `d.min + floor(u*(d.max-d.min+1))` (`medicham2-browser.js:18336`), which is every integer in the span. measured by the driver's own `damage_interior` block and published in `data/game-differential.json`: on one staged hit showdown 14 distinct values, medicham 20, six of which — 110, 113, 116, 119, 122, 125 — the authority can never emit, worst per-value probability gap 7.5 points. every corner instrument is blind to it by construction (the endpoints agree), which is why `test-engine-diff` reads 0/6000. `dmgrangeonehit` already takes a `rolls` out parameter *"in showdown's own `random(16)` index order"* with exactly one caller, so the fix is to select `rolls[index]` instead of interpolating. it moves every damage number in every rollout and wants its own pass and its own probe. fixed 2026-08-18 by engine. it is the support that is wrong, not a rounding stage: 16 indices is a hard ceiling, the randomizer's own floor creates repeats below it (`basedamage/100` per step) and every stage after it — stab `:262`, the type chart `:270-284`, burn `:285`, `modifydamage` `:293` — scales the survivors apart into holes. the loop now selects `rolls[damagerollindex(u)]`. the 14/20 shape holds across a widened fixture of nine staged hits (both categories, a resist, a 4x, an item after the die, two spreads, bp 40-120): ice shard reads 5 authority values against 25, ice beam 9 against 33 — and the two rows whose supports matched still failed the paired clause, so a support count alone understates it. paired, 797 games, `medi_damage_span_draw=1` the only difference: `-damage field 3` 137 -> 8, diverged 409 -> 330, 51.1% -> 41.1%, and both corner arms unmoved at 163/191 — which is the prediction, since `rolls[0]` is `d.max`. the pre arm reproduces #303's published post exactly. standing artifact republished: 969 games, 344 diverged, 2 void, 35.4%. landing it exposed two census probes and one gate clause that were pinning the defect — `spreadfoes` demanded 51, a value the authority cannot emit at any roll; part 3b of `tests/test-game-differential.js` failed if the interior was identical. verified by tests/test-damage-roll-support.js

open.title: CLASS A OF `data/mutation-coverage.json` SAYS "NOTHING IN THE SIMULATOR IMPLEMENTS THIS FACT" AND IT IS WRONG ON AT LEAS
open.full: class a of `data/mutation-coverage.json` says "nothing in the simulator implements this fact" and it is wrong on at least one row i checked by hand — measured 2026-08-22 on release `6fb9ebd3b704`. the a/b/c/d classifier decides a from exactly two things: no `tags.param/has/withtag/reactorsto` call names the tag, and no name branch names the carrier. it does not look at the other tags on the same carrier, and a sibling tag is a third route it cannot see. `move:leechseed / immunitygate` is graded a with the string *"nothing in the simulator implements this fact"*, and the grass immunity is implemented — `medicham2-browser.js:18616` reads `perturnhp.immunetype` and refuses the seed on a grass body. the same shape covers most of the class: `move:lowkick / weightbased` sits beside a read `variablepower {kind:'targetweightkg'}`, `move:acrobatics / readsownitem` beside a read `variablepower {kind:'usernoitem'}`, `move:heatwave / inflictsburn` beside a read `statusinflict`, `move:closecombat / lowersuser` beside a read `statchange`. 31 of the 36 class-a carrier x tag rows carry an armed census probe that proves the mechanic works, which is the artifact telling you the same thing from the other side. the file's own `cannotsee` block says a third route exists; the per-row `defectwhy` contradicts it, and the per-row string is the one that gets read into a report. that is the caption-is-not-a-quarantine failure at row scale. the fix is to the string and to the ranking, not to the rule: a means "this tag is a second, unread copy of the fact", never "this mechanic is missing", and a sibling-tag column belongs in `defectevidence` beside `namebranchat`

`move:fakeout / firstturnonly.{menudisable,whileactivemoveactions}` and `targetclass.*` at 12.44%; `item:lifeorb / damagemultall.costsperattack` at 10.69% — the row rediscovered the expensive way on 2026-08-21 after sitting here for sixteen days; `move:suckerpunch / needstargettoattack.needs` 7.11%; `move:flareblitz|wavecrash / recoil.readfrom` 6.42% and 5.74%; `move:matchagotcha / drain.{num,den}` 4.36% and `move:gigadrain / drain.{num,den}` 1.22%; open.title: THE MUTATION BATTERY PERTURBS PROVENANCE FIELDS AND SCORES THE RESULT AS `READ-AND-IGNORED`, WHICH IS PURE NOISE IN THE
open.full: the mutation battery perturbs provenance fields and scores the result as `read-and-ignored`, which is pure noise in the defect count — measured 2026-08-22. 11 of the 130 shadowed-param rows mutate a field that is not a fact about the game at all: `move:toxic / nevermissesfromusertype.from = "derived:battleactions.prototype.hitstepaccuracy"`, `move:feint|phantomforce / breaksprotect.from`, `move:solarbeam|knockoff / conditionalpower.note = "condition not derivable here -- carried by another tag"`, `ability:levitate / typeimmunity.via = "not derivable -- no handler"`, `ability:earlybird / nameimplementedbysim.{what,cite}`. a `from`/`note`/`cite` field is the tag_dex citation required by the no-typing-from-memory rule; nothing should ever read it, so "mutating it changed nothing" carries no information and inflates read-and-ignored by 11. small, but it is the same class of error as counting a corpse's bookkeeping: the denominator has rows in it that cannot be anything else. skip param names in the provenance set the way `nestedparamsskipped` and `nullparamsskipped` are already skipped — counted, not silent

open.title: THREE MECHANICS ARE GENUINELY ABSENT FROM medicham2 AND ALL THREE ARE WORTH LESS THAN 0.3% OF THE CORPUS — MEASURED 2026
open.full: three mechanics are genuinely absent from medicham2 and all three are worth less than 0.3% of the corpus — measured 2026-08-22, filed so they are not re-discovered, not so they are fixed. after hand-reading every class-a row of `data/mutation-coverage.json` that the census cannot prove (5 of 36), exactly three survive as real gaps and one — `move:leechseed / immunitygate` — is a false positive (see #323). what is real: (a) `immunitygate` on `move:trick` — the simulator contains no lookup for the tag and the string `stickyhold` appears nowhere in it, so trick succeeds against sticky hold; sticky hold has 0 uses in 198,840 corpus sheet entries, and `refusesitemloss`, the other tag that would carry it, is also unread. (b) `punishesminimize` on `move:heavyslam` (467 uses) and `move:bodyslam` (215) — neither the tag nor the string `minimize` appears in the simulator, so the never-miss and the x2 into a minimized body are both absent; minimize is 32 sheet entries, 0.016%, and the mechanic only fires against one. (c) `damagemultonrepeat` on `item:metronome` — the escalating `[4096,4915,5734,6553,7372,8192]` table is unread; 27 sheet entries. the carrier's own usage is the wrong ruler here and it is the trap this row exists to name: heavy slam is clicked 467 times, but the mechanic's reach is minimize's 32, not heavy slam's 467. do not schedule these against #324, which is worth two orders of magnitude more

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE MORPEKO SWITCH DIVERGENCE IS NOT A FORME-DATA GAP AND NOT AN ORDERING ONE — REFUTED WITH A CONTROL, AND THE REAL CAU
open.full: the morpeko switch divergence is not a forme-data gap and not an ordering one — refuted with a control, and the real cause is three defects on one shape. 2026-08-22, engine. #204 was routed on the premise that ten `event missing from medicham2` games name morpeko and that the missing forme rows caused them. three of the 40 cards in `data/divergence-turns.json` mention morpeko and one is the switch case, and it is not a switch order divergence at all: medicham2 emits no line for that slot, which is why the class is `event missing from medicham2`. speed, `comparepriority`, `switchin_order.js` and `data/switchin-order.json` are all irrelevant — those govern the order entry abilities resolve in, not which `|switch|` lines are emitted. refuted: the same board played against two releases identical but for the five forme rows gives byte-identical output. c1, engine — a non-permanent forme change is not reverted when the body leaves the field; measured off the bench, `ours morpeko-hangry` against `the authority morpeko`. showdown's `formechange` takes an `ispermanent` flag, hunger switch passes nothing, `clearvolatile` puts it back. c2, instrument — `game_differential.js` stamps `_switchkey` in `buildpair` (:2213) *precisely* so a rename cannot orphan a body (*“that body can never be switched to again”*), and `freshbodies` (:2362) — what every played game is built from — drops it: `buildpair ["morpeko","dragonite","espathra","garchomp"]` against `freshbodies [null,null,null,null]`. the resolver falls to `id(x.name)`, misses, answers `pass`. one fact, two construction paths, one of them fixed. sufficiency proved without editing the file: restamping from `onboundary` one boundary before the ask brings the subject back. c3, a different defect and said so — a mega is a permanent rename, so both engines hold `abomasnow-mega` while the ask still says `abomasnow`; the showdown branch (:3436) matches on `id(q.species.id)` and misses too, and the game throws rather than diverging. restamping does not clear it. over-fire control: the identical board asked as `{sw:'abomasnowmega'}` completes on both engines. nothing was fixed here on purpose — c1 is in `medicham2-browser.js` (owned by the damage-die agent that day) and c2/c3 are in `game_differential.js`, which is not in `sources` and is therefore read live by every run, so editing it moves a file under a measuring agent. full account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-formes.md`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: TESTING READS A CORPUS THAT MOVES UNDER IT, AND AN ARTIFACT RECORDS WHICH BYTES OF CODE MADE IT BUT NOT WHICH GAMES — WI
open.full: testing reads a corpus that moves under it, and an artifact records which bytes of code made it but not which games — will, 2026-08-17: "lets keep scraping games but for our testing purposes i just want a frozen corpus so it doesnt move". ops appends continuously and should keep doing so — `data/games.bo3.jsonl` and `data/games.ladder.jsonl` both moved at 21:01 on the day this was filed. what must stop moving is what testing reads. two channels leak today. (1) the differential's team pool, already filed as #81 wire 5 and stated in `engine/game_differential.js:4037` in its own words: *"`buildswarm` reads data/games.bo3.jsonl and data/games.ots.jsonl live, dedupes to distinct teams and picks by a stride over the matching set — so one appended game shifts the stride and changes which teams get played"*, with the note that both files moved during that wire's own test runs. the mitigation there asserts which team keys were picked, so a moved pool is visible afterwards; it does not stop the pool moving. `data/team-pool-frozen` already exists and is half the mechanism. (2) every `uses` count, which lives in `data/tags.json` and is regenerated from the live store — two divisions reported it independently on 2026-08-15 as *"~3,271 moved lines are `uses` counts following the store"*. the cost is measured, not hypothetical and not large: the metronome closet entry states 19 uses and the artifact reads 25, with nobody having edited either — the corpus grew underneath a typed number, which is this repository's signature failure in miniature. every impact ranking built on `uses` — the divergence work order, the bring guide, the mechanics priority — is therefore against a moving target at the margin. the second half is the provenance gap and it is the reason nobody noticed: an artifact carries an `engine_release` id saying which bytes of code produced it and nothing saying which games, so two runs can differ entirely in corpus and look identical in provenance. a corpus snapshot id belongs beside the release id in every artifact that reads a game file. not a freeze of the store. ingest keeps running; testing reads a stamped snapshot. sequencing, deliberate: this lands before the mag refit and after the medicham gate closes. the refit is the run that most needs a stable corpus and is the one place where fitting against a moving target would be invisible; doing it before the gate closes would change the corpus definition under an in-flight measurement, which is the failure this row exists to prevent, committed while building the fix

open.title: FUR COAT CARRIES NO DEFENCE MULTIPLIER, SO medicham2 DEALS DOUBLE PHYSICAL DAMAGE THROUGH IT — FOUND 2026-08-21 BY ENGIN
open.full: fur coat carries no defence multiplier, so medicham2 deals double physical damage through it — found 2026-08-21 by engine, by accident, not fixed. furfrou was the first draft of `tests/test-bracket-regain.js`'s second foe and the board parted on the very first physical hit: `p2.party.furfrou.hp medicham 90 showdown 120` on a talonflame facade, medicham dealing exactly double. `data/abra-tags.js` gives `furcoat` a single tag, `breakable`, with no multiplier param at all, so the halving never reaches `dmgrange` — this is a `engine/tag_dex.js` derivation gap and not a missing branch in the simulator, the same shape as #312's sand force, where the derivation read one alternative of a disjunction and the artifact then looked complete. it appeared in all three arms of that file including both controls, so it could not have flipped that verdict, and the cast was changed to a body with an inert ability so `statediv === null` could be asserted rather than excused. 8 corpus sheets, so it is small — and small is exactly the size at which a defect survives, since nothing in the ranked queues will ever surface it. the derivation must be shown its own membership before it is wired: `breakable` is carried by a large family and the multiplier is not, so a predicate that over-matches here would silently halve damage through abilities that do no such thing

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE OPEN-DEFECT CLAUSE CALLS A ROW "NO INSTRUMENT DECIDES IT" WHEN WHAT IT MEANS IS "MY VERDICT ARTIFACT IS OLDER THAN T
open.full: the open-defect clause calls a row "no instrument decides it" when what it means is "my verdict artifact is older than that row" — measured 2026-08-22 on #318 and #319. `engine/where.js --gates` reads `docs/roadmap.md` live and reports that both rows name an instrument. `opendefectclause` in `engine/quarantine.js` reads `data/register-reality.json` and reports both under `debt`, whose line reads *"open row(s) assert breakage with no instrument that decides them"*. both tools are computing the right answer to their own question and one of the two sentences is false. `data/register-reality.json` was generated 2026-08-22t01:55:12z; commit `76e4a67` put the #318 row into the register at 02:33z, thirty-eight minutes later, so the clause has no verdict for a row that has carried a `verified by` marker since it was written. a second, independent cause sits under it: `register_reality.js`'s `safe` guard accepts only a plain `node <repo script>.js [--flags]`, and the marker on both rows begins `showdown_path=... node tests/roster.js --stage moves`, so a fresh run would classify them `instrument unrunnable` rather than giving them a verdict — moving them out of `debt` into the clause's third bucket, never into `withred`. neither reading changes the gate: `ok` is `withred.length === 0`, currently 3 rows (#218, #241, #258) out of 16 open-and-asserting-breakage, and `debt` has never held the clause shut. the defect is the bookkeeping, and `where.js` already does its half: since commit `cac12fa` it prints *"naming a gate is not having a verdict"*, names the artifact's age, and lists the rows with no verdict. the quarantine side says nothing. what would decide it: `opendefectclause` reads the row it is already parsing for a `verified by` marker and splits `debt` into "names nothing" and "names an instrument, no verdict recorded", and compares `register-reality.json`'s `generated` against the mtime of `docs/roadmap.md`, printing stale when the artifact is older. related and not the same row: #108 is `status.js` against `provenance.js` over artifact safety; this is the open-defect clause against `where.js` over the register's own coverage. same shape, second pair — which is itself the argument for fixing the shape rather than the instance. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-register-reconciliation.md`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE DIVERGENCE ROLLUP'S RANKING CAN NAME THE LINE WE EMITTED RATHER THAN THE ONE THAT DIFFERS, AND A HUMAN READING 40 CA
open.full: the divergence rollup's ranking can name the line we emitted rather than the one that differs, and a human reading 40 cards found ~20 root causes where the rollup over the same run found none — measured 2026-08-22. the class name describes the comparator, not the defect. `event missing from medicham2` means "the authority emitted a line and we did not", which is a property of the diff and is the same sentence whether the cause is encore's failure condition, imposter's transform announcement or a life orb recoil. two defects with nothing in common land in one bucket and one defect lands in several depending on which line differed first, so the rollup can only ever report how the comparator classified things. over the same 961-game run its buckets were *"`-fail` 7 games"* and *"ordering 29 games"*; will grouped by mechanism instead and recognised encore, roost, toxic debris and matcha gotcha on sight. two concrete ranking defects. (1) `max_uses` is `math.max` over the entities named by both lines of a pair, so the head of a usage-ordered list can name the line we emitted: the report's own head read *"126,170 clicks, protect"* when the differing line was `-start|typechange|[from] protean`. that half is confirmed against the current file — `entitystanding` collects mentions from both sides and `max_uses` is a max over all of them. (2) the card review also records a species carrying `uses: null` printed as 0, putting the kingambit `fallen` family at the bottom of a usage-ordered list while covering 31.4% of games; that half is not confirmed against the current file — a `species_uses` block reading `data/meta-usage.json` exists and may already supply it, and the observation may predate it or belong to a different renderer. recorded as observed-and-unconfirmed rather than asserted. the action will asked for is cheaper than either fix: dump far more cards. `--dump-games 40` sampled 40 of 378 diverging games; a card costs a few hundred bytes and a missed root cause costs an evening. raise it to the low hundreds and render with `engine/divergence_cards.js`. what would decide it: print the ranking key beside each cause — which entity, from which side's line — so a reader can see whether the head names the divergent line or ours

open.title: THE ROSTER CREDITS SPIKY SHIELD ON A SCENARIO THAT CANNOT FAIL — OBSERVED 2026-08-22, INSTRUMENT WEAKNESS, MECHANIC BELI
open.full: the roster credits spiky shield on a scenario that cannot fail — observed 2026-08-22, instrument weakness, mechanic believed covered elsewhere. `all_mechanics_fire` reports `spikyshield` as resolved / no-divergence with `setup: []` — nothing attacks into it — and marks both `volatile:spikyshield` and `volatile:stall` uncomparable. so `punishescontact` (`oncontact: true, fraction: 8`, correctly derived) never fires in that row, and a green there is a green about nothing. the mechanic itself is well covered and this row is not a claim that it is broken: 40 census rows touch protect/shield/stall, including *"spiky shield hurts the attacker it blocked"* with a protect control that must toll 0 while spiky shield tolls 22, *"a spiky shield answers before the type chart"*, and *"spiky shield and baneful bunker refuse encore exactly as protect does"* for the status half (#238). the census is the strong instrument; the roster row is the weak one. note also that the authority itself announces spiky shield as `move: protect` on both `-singleturn` and `-activate`, so our naming there is correct and the renderer is faithful — that is not a defect and is recorded here so it is not filed as one later. what would decide it: the roster's scenario builder must refuse to credit a mechanic whose `setup` is empty, or must stage a contact attacker into the shield; a row that cannot fail is a test that cannot fail, which is #314's lesson applied to a different instrument. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §f2

open.title: `tools/lownode.cmd` IS SOUND AND ITS ARGUMENT QUOTING IS A LIVE HAZARD THAT HAS ALREADY TRUNCATED A RELEASE REASON — OBS
open.full: `tools/lownode.cmd` is sound and its argument quoting is a live hazard that has already truncated a release reason — observed 2026-08-22. the wrapper itself passes: `tests/test-lownode.js` is 4/4 including exit-code propagation, and measured directly it returned 7 for `process.exit(7)` and 1 for a module-not-found with stdout and stderr intact. the hazard is the arguments. an absolute windows path splits on its drive colon across the bash-to-`cmd` boundary, and `start` mis-parses a quoted argument containing spaces — `--seed "a vs b"` launches `cmd` rather than `node`. it has already cost something: a quoted `--why` string was truncated to a fragment on an engine-release cut, so a release carries a reason that is not the reason anybody typed. the workaround is repo-relative paths and no spaces in a quoted argument, and that is a rule somebody has to remember, which is what this register exists to replace. what would decide it: an arm in `tests/test-lownode.js` that passes an argument containing a space and an argument containing a drive-letter path and asserts the child received them byte-identically — shown red against the current wrapper before any change. related and not the same: #300, the differential's unreachable catch block on a bad `showdown_path`. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §f3

open.title: THE AUTHORITY ANNOUNCES A VOLATILE COUNTER'S EXPIRY AND WE ARE SILENT, AND NOTHING PROVES THE TWO ENGINES END ON THE SAM
open.full: the authority announces a volatile counter's expiry and we are silent, and nothing proves the two engines end on the same turn — observed 2026-08-22 by will across three cards. three cards, three counters, one question: do they tick and expire on the same turn? showdown emits `-end ... infestation [partiallytrapped] [silent]` twice and `-end ... throat chop` once, and we emit nothing. the state behind them is compared — `board_state.js:661` reads `trapped_by_move`, and the file notes the victim's half is *"the half that decides whether a switch is legal"* — but the comparator's own proof is not clean: `probe_bench_plants.js` lists a move trap counter off by one among its 19 applied-and-not-caught plants (7 of 8 pairs catch it), which is #314's second hole. so the field is read, a lie about it is mostly detected, and the instrument cannot say so with authority. an unannounced expiry at the right moment is cosmetic; one a turn late is a body that cannot switch when it should. infestation blocks switching, and perish song's last tick kills — `duration: 4`, the cast-time `perish3` is `[silent]`, and the residual prints whatever the counter now reads, one step per end of turn. not covered by #242, which is closed and settled the residual order and which of 90 walk participants announce; and not covered by #234, closed, which fixed the `[from]` attribution naming the condition where showdown names the move. neither asserts that a counter expires on the same turn. what would decide it: stage infestation, throat chop and perish song separately, run each to expiry on both engines, and assert both end on the same turn and emit the same `-end` line — with perish song's arm asserting the body dies on the same turn, since that is the one where a tick off by one is a game

open.title: A FAILED ROOST LEAVES THE USER STILL FLYING ON THE AUTHORITY AND GROUNDED HERE, AND IT IS BOARD-MATERIAL — STAGED AND DE
open.full: a failed roost leaves the user still flying on the authority and grounded here, and it is board-material — staged and deliberately not fixed 2026-08-22. found while landing #342's `null`-against-`false` classification and stated in that commit's own account, with no register row until now. we emit the `-fail ... heal` line correctly and then also the `-singleturn`; the authority emits neither, because `runmoveeffects` marks the target `false` and `selfdrops` skips false targets. the consequence is not the two lines: it is that the roost user's flying type is suppressed here on a turn the authority leaves it flying, so a ground move that should be refused connects, and every damage and speed read for that turn is taken against the wrong type. left undone on purpose — the rule in this repository is one family per pass, and the roost family wants its own hand list rather than a free ride inside the encore/yawn batch. what would decide it: stage a roost that fails (a user already at full hp) on both engines and assert (a) neither line is emitted and (b) a ground move into that user is refused on both. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §e3 and commit `11bab14`. adjacent: #147 wired roost's grounding in the first place; #242 records that roost is residual order 25, announces nothing, and gives its type back twenty orders above the grassy terrain heal
