open.title: DRAGON TAIL AND CIRCLE THROW IGNORE SUCTION CUPS — CONFIRMED, PROBED RED 2026-08-22. The phaze branch reads `refusesForc
open.full: dragon tail and circle throw ignore suction cups — confirmed, probed red 2026-08-22. the phaze branch reads `refusesforcedswitch`; the damaging branch does not, so a damaging phaze move drags a body the authority refuses to move. staged: tyranitar's dragon tail into malamar — the authority emits `-activate p2a: malamar / ability: suction cups` and nobody moves; we emit a `drag` of snorlax. malamar is the only legal carrier of suction cups in reg m-b and is brought 1,340 times across the two human stores. the membership is derived and small, which is why it can be closed cleanly: exactly two abilities and one move carry `ondragout` in the whole authority — suction cups (legal, one carrier), guard dog (zero legal carriers) and ingrain (a legal move that zero legal species can learn here). champions overrides none of the three. that is why this is the only member of the family that can fire, and it is why #175's rule holds: do not add a guard dog row by hand — `tests/test-tag-params-derived.js` proves the predicate already covers it, its absence is the legality filter, and a regulation that brings a carrier would pick it up with no edit. what would decide it: the staged tyranitar-into-malamar pair above, asserting no body moves and the `-activate` line is present, with a non-carrier control that must still be dragged

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE BENCH IS IN A DIFFERENT ORDER FROM THE AUTHORITY'S, AND BOTH OF OUR INSTRUMENTS ARE BLIND TO IT BY CONSTRUCTION — DI
open.full: the bench is in a different order from the authority's, and both of our instruments are blind to it by construction — diagnosed 2026-08-22, die hypothesis refuted, landed as a diagnosis with no row until now. the drag divergence was hypothesised to be the die and it is not: both engines roll a uniform die, consume exactly one draw, and under pinned dice draw the same value at the same address. what differs is the order of the list the die indexes into. `sim/battle-actions.ts:125-132` swaps the outgoing body into the arriving body's party slot; we remove-and-append. measured: 34.8% of side-boundaries hold the same bench in a different order, and 0 of 3,118 index positions map to the same body — zero fixed points, so a uniform index disagrees with probability 1. invisible to both instruments, and that is the important part: the protocol comparison sees no line, and `board_state.js`'s `partymap` keys the party by species — correctly, because index-keying manufactured a divergence in 123 of 179 games — and the same correct choice makes it blind to where a body is standing. blast radius is larger than the drag: `bringin`'s default replacement is `_live(bench)[0]`, so a reordered bench moves every faint replacement and every pivot with no explicit target, in rollouts and in `board.js` features. measure it; do not assume it neutral. what would decide it: a boundary-by-boundary comparison of the two party arrays by index (not by species) on a pinned run, asserting the same body stands at the same index, with the 3,118 positions as the denominator. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §e1; the diagnosis landed in commit `11bab14` and carried no register row

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: LIFE ORB RECOIL DID NOT FIRE FOR A WHOLE TURN IN A REAL GAME, WHICH IS THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF #324 EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES — O
open.full: life orb recoil did not fire for a whole turn in a real game, which is the behavioural half #324 explicitly excludes — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 24 (index 37); not probed since. `data/tags.json` gives `lifeorb` a `damagemultall` of `mult 1.3` plus `costsperattack: "1/10 max hp"` — the multiplier is machine-readable and the cost is an english string, so nothing can derive the recoil from the tag and whatever applies it is hardcoded elsewhere, which is why it fires in two cards and not in a third. on this card gholdengo landed a resisted shadow ball and never paid its 16 hp; the stream runs to the `upkeep` marker with no life orb line at all, so it is absent for the turn, not merely late. life orb appears in 17,168 of 19,401 bo3 games and the roster credits it `fired / diverged false`, so two live instruments both call it clean. not covered by #324, and the distinction is the point: #324 registers `item:lifeorb / damagemultall.costsperattack` as one of 119 tag values read by nothing and says in its own words that *"none of these is a behavioural defect on its own — the mutation moved nothing"*. this row is the counterexample to that sentence for one member of the 119. what would decide it: replay card 24's index 37 on both engines and assert the recoil line is present, then stage a resisted hit, a super-effective hit and a hit that would leave the holder at 1 hp — a recoil applied conditionally is what the two-of-three card pattern suggests

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A SPREAD DRAIN HEALS ONCE OVER THE SUMMED DAMAGE WHERE THE AUTHORITY HEALS AND ROUNDS PER TARGET, SO WE HEAL 1 HP LESS O
open.full: a spread drain heals once over the summed damage where the authority heals and rounds per target, so we heal 1 hp less on a quarter of them — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 1 (index 0). showdown heals per target, interleaved, with an `[of]` attribution on each; we heal once at the end and drop the attribution. the arithmetic is merged too, and that half is not narration: `dealt` accumulates across targets and the drain heals half of the accumulated total once, where the authority rounds per target (`battle.ts:2168`). the two disagree exactly when both hits deal odd damage — 25.0% of two-target spread drains — and we heal 1 hp less. legal spread-drain moves in this regulation: matcha gotcha (8,182 uses) and parabolic charge (151); parabolic charge is `alladjacent`, so up to three drains and three roundings. partially adjacent to #324, which lists `move:matchagotcha / drain.{num,den}` at 4.36% of corpus sheet entries as a param the simulator dereferences nowhere — that is the derivation half; this is the arithmetic half and #324 asserts nothing about it. what would decide it: a staged two-target matcha gotcha whose per-target damage is odd on both bodies, asserting the healer's hp matches the authority to the point, with an even-damage control that must agree both before and after the fix

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `onTryImmunity` IS NOT DERIVED, SO SIX LEGAL MOVES CARRY NO IMMUNITY GATE AT ALL — OBSERVED 2026-08-22 BY WILL READING C
open.full: `ontryimmunity` is not derived, so six legal moves carry no immunity gate at all — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 35. endeavor's gate is `ontryimmunity(target, pokemon) { return pokemon.hp < target.hp; }`, and returning false produces a type-immunity-style block (`-immune`), not `-fail`. on card 35 both bodies were at 135/135 — whimsicott and raichu share max hp at l50 and 0 ev — so `135 < 135` is false and the authority answered `-immune`; we ran the `damagecallback` (`target.hp - pokemon.hp` = 0) and announced a zero-damage line reading "drops to 100%". our tags for `endeavor` carry no immunity condition at all. legal moves on this hook: attract, endeavor, leech seed, switcheroo, trick, worry seed. trick and switcheroo matter most — a missing immunity gate means an item swap that should be blocked goes through, which is board-material. recurring shape: a fact that lives in a handler rather than a declarative field is not picked up by `tag_dex`, and the roster then credits the entity clean because nothing staged the condition — joins #317 (fur coat) and #312 (sand force). adjacent and not the same rows: #327 covers `immunitygate` on `move:trick` against sticky hold specifically (0 corpus uses), and #323 records `move:leechseed / immunitygate` as a classifier false positive because the grass immunity is implemented through a sibling tag. neither covers the hook. will's requirement, and it is the discipline that got the last `-fail` attempt retracted: stage the positive arm too. three cases, all three asserted: user hp greater than target hp gives `-immune` with no damage line; user hp equal to target hp gives `-immune` as well, because the gate is a strict less-than (the 135/135 case, easy to miss); user hp less than target hp works, the target drops to exactly the user's hp with a real `-damage` line. a test that only proves the immunity is a test that ships an endeavor which never works

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: SLEEP: THE DISTRIBUTION IS MODELLED CORRECTLY AND WHETHER THE DRAW IS ADDRESSED IDENTICALLY HAS NEVER BEEN CHECKED — RAI
open.full: sleep: the distribution is modelled correctly and whether the draw is addressed identically has never been checked — raised 2026-08-22, verification owed, no claim of breakage made. champions overrides `slp` and uses `this.sample([2, 3, 3])` (*"1/3 chance for a pokemon to wake up on turn 2"*) where mainline uses `this.random(2, 5)` giving 2, 3 or 4 — a different distribution and a different draw shape, since `sample` calls `random(3)`. our `sleep_turns_lost = 1 + 2/3` is exactly the expected value of `sample([2,3,3])`, one third times one plus two thirds times two, so the distribution half is right. what is unverified is the address: whether both engines consume the same number of draws at the same point, which is what decides every later die in a pinned game. reading mainline here is the documented way to be wrong. what would decide it: a pinned staged sleep on both engines printing the draw count and the address consumed, against the champions override read from the mod and cited by line. this row asserts nothing about a mechanic being wrong and deliberately carries no defect token in its cell: a row that overstates its scope costs a whole agent, which is more than the defect it names

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE CONFUSION SELF-HIT DRAWS A DIFFERENT INDEX FROM THE AUTHORITY, AND THE FORMULA IS RULED OUT AS THE CAUSE — OBSERVED
open.full: the confusion self-hit draws a different index from the authority, and the formula is ruled out as the cause — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 36; root cause unprobed. our formula is correct and documented: no stab, no type chart, no crit, no screen, no burn, sixteen sides at `85+r`, matching `getconfusiondamage` (`battle-actions.ts:1850`), with one gap declared rather than hidden — an `onmodifyatk` ability, so a burned guts body hits itself harder. the move is typed with the wildcard category, so no item or type boost can reach it; that hypothesis is ruled out. authority `108 -> 75` against our `108 -> 78` is 33 against 30, and `30/33 = 0.909` sits inside the 85-100% band, so it is a different index, not a different multiplier. note the authority takes two draws here — `randomchance(33,100)` for whether to self-hit, then `randomizer(damage)` — so a different order or category shifts every later die address too, and this may be an addressing defect rather than a damage one. what would decide it: pin the dice and print the index each engine selected for the same staged self-hit, plus the draw count consumed at that address. do not fold this into #333 until the index is read: one is a scheme and the other is an address

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A PER-TARGET SECONDARY LANDS ON THE WRONG BODY — #294 FIXED THE ACCURACY ROLL AND NOT THE SECONDARY ROLL. OBSERVED 2026-
open.full: a per-target secondary lands on the wrong body — #294 fixed the accuracy roll and not the secondary roll. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 40; not probed since. muddy water is a spread move with a 30% accuracy-drop secondary that the authority rolls per target. showdown dropped spiritomb's accuracy; we dropped snorlax's. same shape as #294 — *"the accuracy roll was one per move where the game rolls one per target"* — one hook over, and #294 is closed, so its row must not be read as covering this. the sleep difference in the same card is probably downstream of this: once a secondary fires on a different body every later die address shifts, so it must not be treated as an independent defect until this is fixed. what would decide it: a scripted per-target secondary stream on a spread move with a sub-100% secondary, asserting all four outcomes (neither, first only, second only, both) are reachable — the exact discriminator #294 used for the accuracy roll, shown red on the pre-fix tree there, and never run for secondaries

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE MULTI-HIT DAMAGE PATH WAS NEVER CONVERTED TO THE SIXTEEN-INDEX ROLL, SO #304'S FIX COVERS SINGLE HITS ONLY — PROVED
open.full: the multi-hit damage path was never converted to the sixteen-index roll, so #304's fix covers single hits only — proved by arithmetic 2026-08-22 from cards 38 and 39. `battle#randomizer` is `tr(tr(base * (100 - random(16))) / 100)`: sixteen discrete values between 85% and 100% of the base. twin beam is the clean case because both hits are 40 bp, so the base is identical for both. authority `185 -> 130 -> 75`, hits of 55 and 55 — one base, the same index twice. medicham2 `185 -> 125 -> 75`, hits of 60 and 50. no single base can produce both under that scheme: 60 requires `b >= 60` and 50 requires `trunc(b x 0.85) <= 50`, i.e. `b < 60`. contradiction. so either our base changes between hits of a constant-bp move or our draw is not the sixteen-index one. this is the unconverted residue of #304, whose own status cell already names it — *"8 games survive, candidate is the declared per-hit multi-hit randomizer"* — and a uniform draw would produce 60 and 50 from one base because it can hit any integer in the interval. it also explains will's observation that multi-hit damage "evens out": a uniform draw is unbiased about the same mean, so totals converge while individual hits scatter. what would decide it: a staged constant-bp two-hit move on both engines under pinned dice, asserting the two hits are equal whenever the authority's two are equal, plus a per-hit support count in the style of #304's `damage_interior` block

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `onDamagingHit` IS WRONG TWICE ON ONE HOOK — IT RESOLVES BEFORE THE MOVE'S OWN SECONDARIES WHERE THE AUTHORITY RESOLVES
open.full: `ondamaginghit` is wrong twice on one hook — it resolves before the move's own secondaries where the authority resolves it after, and it fires once per move where the authority fires once per hit. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading divergence cards 29 and 37; not probed since. two defects, filed as one row because they are one derivation. order: `sim/battle-actions.ts:1099` runs `secondaries()` and `:1121` runs `runevent('damaginghit')`, so secondaries resolve first; card 29 is flare blitz's burn against a stamina defense boost in the opposite order here. frequency: card 37 has the authority laying one toxic debris layer per hit of dual wingbeat where we lay one after the move completes. twenty legal abilities ride this hook — aftermath, cursed body, cute charm, effect spore, electromorphosis, flame body, gooey, illusion, innards out, justified, mummy, poison point, rough skin, sand spit, spicy spray, stamina, static, toxic debris, wandering spirit, weak armor — and several are board-material rather than cosmetic: aftermath and innards out deal damage, so the attacker's hp when the secondary lands differs; weak armor changes speed and therefore turn order; cursed body disables a move; and mummy overwrites the attacker's ability, so running it before a secondary the new ability would have modified resolves that secondary under the wrong ability entirely. what would decide it: two staged pairs run on both engines — (a) a contact flare blitz into a stamina carrier, asserting the same relative order of the burn and the boost, and (b) a two-hit contact move into a toxic debris carrier, asserting two layers rather than one. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §a1, release `6a05dd9ad60d`, census pin `2cab3179f5fc`, 961 games / 133 diverged

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `onSwitchInPriority` IS NOT MODELLED AT ALL — WE SORT SWITCH-IN EFFECTS BY SPEED AND THE AUTHORITY SORTS BY A DECLARED P
open.full: `onswitchinpriority` is not modelled at all — we sort switch-in effects by speed and the authority sorts by a declared per-ability priority first. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading cards 26 and 27; not probed since. `battle#comparepriority` is order, then priority, then speed — speed is only the third tiebreak — and this engine sorts entry effects on speed alone. sixteen abilities declare the field in mainline, champions overrides none, and five have legal carriers in reg m-b: unnerve `+1` (6 carriers incl. tyranitar), klutz `+1` (3), mimicry `-1` (1, stunfisk-galar), forecast `-2` (4, castform + formes), hospitality `-2` (2, sinistcha and sinistcha-masterpiece). card 26 is the proof and it runs the wrong way round from speed: torkoal is base-20 speed and sinistcha base-70, yet drought fired first on the authority because hospitality carries `-2`. we put the faster body first and got the reverse. same family as the intimidate-vs-drizzle card. what would decide it: a staged entry pair on both engines with a hospitality carrier faster than a weather setter, asserting the weather setter resolves first; plus the derived membership printed before wiring, because a name-matched implementation of five carriers is the shape this repository bans. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §a2

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: WE ANNOUNCE A FAINT AT THE MOMENT OF LETHAL DAMAGE AND THE AUTHORITY BATCHES IT UNTIL THE ACTION COMPLETES. OBSERVED 202
open.full: we announce a faint at the moment of lethal damage and the authority batches it until the action completes. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading cards 28 and 34; not probed since. `this.add('faint', pokemon)` lives inside `faintmessages()` (`sim/battle.ts:2549`), which `runaction` calls at `:2832` after the action finishes, so showdown completes the move's own consequences — the recharge flag, stone axe's hazard, fling's item — and announces deaths afterwards. two consequences beyond the ordering itself. (1) `faintmessages(lastfirst = false, …)`: the `lastfirst` argument is why final gambit faints the user before the target on the authority and the reverse here. (2) it also explains a wording difference for free — `pokemon#tostring()` returns `p2a: name` while active and bare `p2: name` once not, and `faintmessages` sets `isactive = false` at `:2563`, so the authority's `-hitcount` names an already-dead body (`p2: azumarill`) where ours names a live one (`p2a: azumarill`). one root, two visible symptoms. likely worth more than its card count: a faint announced early shifts every line after it, so games currently filed under other classes may be downstream of this one. imposter (#320) predicted ~10 and delivered 13 for exactly that reason. what would decide it: stage a lethal stone axe and a lethal final gambit on both engines and assert the `|faint|` line's position relative to the hazard line and to the target's faint. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §a3. adjacent and not the same row: #315, a fainted mega's forme regression, which is the other half of the same `faintmessages` region

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A BERRY IS EATEN BEFORE the `upkeep` MARKER AND\|upkeep` AND BEFORE FAINT PROCESSING HERE, AND AFTER BOTH IN THE AUTHORI
open.full: a berry is eaten before the `upkeep` marker and\|upkeep` and before faint processing here, and after both in the authority — this one changes who survives. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 30; not probed since. the authority's residual case runs `fieldevent('residual')`, then `add('upkeep')`, then `faintmessages()`, and only then `eachevent('update')` — and sitrus hooks `onupdate`, so it eats after the turn-end marker and after deaths are processed. we eat during the residual sequence. two ways that moves the board rather than the narration. (a) a body that residual damage would kill is dead before the berry can be eaten on the authority; eating mid-sequence heals it above zero and it lives. (b) with several residuals in sequence, eating mid-sequence gives a larger hp pool to every residual that follows — body at 20, poison 15 then sandstorm 7: authority 20 -> 5 -> 0 dead, ours 20 -> 5 -> berry 36 -> 29 alive. the residual order itself is checked and correct and is not part of this row: `data/residual-order.json` carries sandstorm at order 1 / `onfieldresidual` and leftovers at order 5 / suborder 4, derived from the authority, and the simulator reads the numbers from that file rather than hardcoding them (#221, #242). will raised this as the ko-flipping hazard; the residual half is sound and the berry half is where it bites. what would decide it: stage a sitrus holder at an hp the residual chain exactly kills, on both engines, and assert the body is dead on both. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §a4

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: MOODY RAISES AND DROPS DIFFERENT STATS FROM THE AUTHORITY IN 8 OF THE 121 WHOLE-GAME DIVERGENCES, AND THE INSTRUMENT CAN
open.full: moody raises and drops different stats from the authority in 8 of the 121 whole-game divergences, and the instrument cannot say whether the two engines even share the die — filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. observed on `data/game-differential.json`, release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z: six causes in `-boost field 3` and two in `-unboost field 3`, e.g. `\|-boost\|p2a\|spa\|2 <> \|-boost\|p2a\|def\|2` and `\|-unboost\|p1a\|spa\|1 <> \|-unboost\|p1a\|spe\|1`. the magnitudes agree on every one — both sides chose a raise and a drop and only the stat identity parts — so this is selection, not clamping. both selection rules were read and they agree, which is what makes the draw the live question. the authority is `data/abilities.ts:2691-2719` (champions does not override `moody`): two `this.sample` draws, the first over boosts `< 6`, the second over boosts `> -6` excluding the stat just raised, both skipping accuracy and evasion, iterating `pokemon.boosts` in key order atk, def, spa, spd, spe. ours is `engine/medicham2-browser.js:23030-23042`: `_st=['at','df','sa','sd','sp']`, the same two predicates, `math.floor(rng()*l.length)`. same membership, same order, same number of draws, same mapping. two claims the wire-queue triage made for this mechanic did not survive a check. (1) its corroboration was the roster reading `fired-and-boards-differ`; `data/roster.abilities.json`, generated 2026-08-22t19:08:07z on the same release as the differential, now reads `fired-and-boards-match` with a second control (ice body) that found *"the two deltas differ on 28 leaf/leaves, which means at least one control is live on this fixture … 24 of 38 leaf/leaves survive both controls and the verdict is computed on those alone."* the differ was a live control. (2) *"under the middle arm's pinned dice both engines draw the same value at the same address"* is not supported: `engine/game_differential.js` wraps exactly three authority methods to derive a category — `hitstepaccuracy` → `acc`, `secondaries` → `sec`, `getdamage` → `dmg` — and a residual ability draw executes in none of them. the artifact agrees from its own side: every entry of `mid_void.unshared_address_shapes` is `acc`, `crit` or `dmg`. so this may be the instrument rather than the engine, which is the morpeko shape (#328, two of three causes were the harness), and no verdict is filed. what would decide it: print the address each side uses for the moody residual draw on one staged residual and compare — extend the category wrapper past the three `battleactions` methods, or publish that a residual draw is unshared. a stat-selection probe means nothing until that is answered

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE `\|-weather\|W\|[upkeep]` LINE IS GATED ON A SUPPRESSION FLAG THE AUTHORITY NEVER CONSULTS — THE GATE IS A DERIVED D
open.full: the `\|-weather\|w\|[upkeep]` line is gated on a suppression flag the authority never consults — the gate is a derived defect and it probably does not explain its own five games. filed 2026-08-22 by measure. five of the 121 (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `\|-weather\|raindance\|[upkeep] <> \|upkeep` ×4 and one sandstorm. the authority emits it unconditionally: `data/conditions.ts:504-508`, `onfieldresidualorder: 1, onfieldresidual() { this.add('-weather','raindance','[upkeep]'); this.eachevent('weather'); }`, and champions does not override it — `data/mods/champions/conditions.ts` contains no `raindance`, no `sandstorm` and no `onfieldresidual`. ours is gated: `engine/medicham2-browser.js:22880` — `if(tr){if(field.weather&&!field.wsup)tr.wx(field.weather,null,null,true);else if(_wx0&&!field.weather)tr.wxnone();}`. a gate the authority does not have is a defect on its own terms: under a suppressor we go silent where the authority still writes the line. but the five games are not attributed to it, and the alternative is worse than an announcement. `suppressesweather(m)` is `tags.param('ability',m.ability,'weathersuppression')` and `cloudnine` is the only carrier of that param in `data/tags.json`; i read the four actives in each of the five games and none carries it — raichu/starmie/annihilape/sneasler, archaludon/venusaur/whimsicott/raichu, greninja/gengar/archaludon/kingambit, maushold/pelipper/farigiraf/heracross. if `wsup` is false then the else-branch decides, and it emits nothing only when `_wx0` is also falsy — a sky that is already gone on our side, with no `\|-weather\|none` ever emitted, which is board-material (the rain multipliers, swift swim, thunder) and not narration. two of the five sit at `agreed_lines: 17`, turn 2, immediately after all four actives switched out, and in a third the rain was set by a pelipper drizzle inside the agreed prefix — so our engine did have the sky. what would decide it: stage rain from drizzle, switch the setter out, and read `field.weather` and `field.weathert` on both engines on the following turn; then a separate one-line arm with a cloud nine body for the gate itself

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A `\|switch\|` LINE IS ORDERED BY THE DEPARTING BODY'S SPEED IN THE AUTHORITY, AND NOTHING PUBLISHES WHETHER WE AGREE —
open.full: a `\|switch\|` line is ordered by the departing body's speed in the authority, and nothing publishes whether we agree — 3 of the 121, filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. causes (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `ordering :: \|switch\|p1b\|whimsicott,l50\|h/h <> \|switch\|p1a\|alakazam,l50\|h/h` (turn 2, a same-side double switch), `\|switch\|p1a\|staraptor <> \|switch\|p2a\|incineroar`, `\|switch\|p1a\|palafin <> \|move\|p2b\|helpinghand`. the authority's key is derived and verified line by line: `sim/battle-queue.ts:270` `if (!deferpriority) this.battle.getactionspeed(action);` → `sim/battle.ts:2657` `action.speed = action.pokemon.getactionspeed();`, and `switchaction` documents its own fields at `sim/battle-queue.ts:56-69` — `pokemon` is *"the pokemon doing the switch"* (the outgoing body) and `target` is *"pokemon to switch to"*. not covered by #330: #328 says in as many words that `switchin_order.js` governs entry ability order and not which `\|switch\|` lines are emitted. and an instrument gap found while looking, which is why no verdict is filed: this engine already declares an approximation on exactly this axis — `medfails.entryordertie` and `medfails.replaceordertie` (`medicham2-browser.js:1866-1874`), *"showdown shuffles the instaswitch pair; this engine keeps side order and counts the event, because drawing a number here would move the rng stream of every seeded run in the repo"* — and neither counter is published in `data/game-differential.json`, so the artifact cannot tell a declared tie from an ordering defect. what would decide it: publish the two counters in the run, then stage two double-switches with a known speed spread and assert the `\|switch\|` line order extended 2026-08-23 onto the settled artifact: on release `c66976713feb` (961 games, generated 2026-08-23t02:40:37z, triage `ea26208`) this class is 5, not 3. the two new causes — `ordering :: \|switch\|p1a\|garchomp <> \|switch\|p2b\|blastoise` and `\|switch\|p1a\|swampert <> \|switch\|p2a\|delphox` — are both post-faint replacements, and the second refutes a naive reading from inside the file: the authority moved the slower side first, so replacements do not go in speed order of the incoming body. four of the five carry `max_uses: null` — the mentions are species and species have no `uses` — so a usage-ordered head buries this group while it fires on every double switch and every post-faint replacement. the unpublished-counter ask above is still unmet and is now carried by #375 as well.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: WE FLINCH WHERE THE AUTHORITY MOVES — 2 OF THE 121, AND THIS ONE IS INSIDE THE ARM'S ADDRESSED SET. FILED 2026-08-22 BY
open.full: we flinch where the authority moves — 2 of the 121, and this one is inside the arm's addressed set. filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. two causes (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `\|-immune\|p1b <> \|cant\|p2a\|flinch` and `unrelated event mismatch :: \|move\|p2a\|psychicfangs <> \|cant\|p2a\|flinch`. in the second the authority's metagross uses psychic fangs and ours cannot act, so it is board-material in both directions — a turn of damage that does or does not happen. unlike #351 a shared-die argument is available here: the flinch chance is rolled in `secondaries`, which is one of the three methods `engine/game_differential.js` wraps for its address (`sec`), so the two engines are drawing at an addressed site and identity is measurable. #84 is not this — that is the `false`-against-`null` question and it is closed. what would decide it: fake out into a body under the same pinned `sec` stream, and assert `\|cant\|…\|flinch` fires on both engines or on neither

open.title: TWO TAILWINDS EXPIRING ON THE SAME TURN COME OUT IN THE OPPOSITE ORDER, AND #242 SETTLED WHERE IN THE WALK RATHER THAN W

open.title: THE 22 DAMAGING `self` MOVES FAIL THROUGH A DOOR THAT HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED, AND THE DECLARATION LIVED ONLY IN A CHANG
open.full: the 22 damaging `self` moves fail through a door that has never been measured, and the declaration lived only in a changelog — filed 2026-08-23 by measure, no verdict. #343 staged the one heal-primary status member (a failed roost, where we emit the `-fail` and then also the `-singleturn` and ground a body the authority leaves flying) and that pass declared the rest open rather than sweeping them in — correct, the scope of a fix is the scope that was probed. but the declaration existed only in changelog 5.74.0 and in no register row, which is the same failure as a figure that lives only in prose: nothing could print it, so nothing could act on it. membership derived from the format tonight, filtered to the regulation, not typed: 25 legal moves carry a `self` effect; 3 are status — baton pass, roost, shed tail — and exactly one of those is heal-primary (roost, `self.heal` true); 22 are damaging. ten carry `self.boosts` (close combat, superpower, hammer arm, ice hammer, headlong rush, draco meteor, leaf storm, overheat, make it rain, armor cannon), eleven `self.volatilestatus` (hyper beam, giga impact, outrage, thrash, petal dance, raging fury, uproar, blast burn, hydro cannon, frenzy plant, rock wrecker), one `self.onhit` (burn up). this is not a tail: 32,135 clicks of 424,933 in the clean corpus — 7.6% — and close combat alone is 18,600, with draco meteor 3,291, make it rain 2,811, overheat 1,879 and hyper beam 1,708. the door is the one #343 found: `runmoveeffects` writes `damage[i] = false` on a refused hit, `spreadmovehit` sets `targets[i] = false`, and step 4 `selfdrops` skips a false target — so for each of the 22 the open question is whether our self-rider fires on a hit the authority refused (a protect, a type immunity, a miss, a substitute). for the ten boost members that is a stat stage that does or does not exist; for the eleven volatile members it is whether the user is locked or recharging, which decides the whole of the following turn. nothing here claims they are wrong. the failure path has not been measured on any of the 22, on either engine, and no `defect` token is filed — an unprobed member is not a defect, and calling it one would corrupt the open-defect clause exactly as much as missing a real one. what would decide it: one staged pair per `self` shape rather than per move — close combat into a protect asserting the defence drop on both engines or on neither; hyper beam into a ghost asserting `mustrecharge` on both or on neither, which is the board #161 records wire 43 getting backwards once already; burn up into a target that refuses it for the `onhit` shape. three probes cover 22 members, and the shapes are derived, not listed. instrument owed: one staged pair per `self` shape — boosts, volatilestatus, onhit — asserting the self-rider fires on both engines or on neither when the authority refused the hit.

the file is under active engine edit — grep the symbol) writes it unconditionally in the swarm block, under its own comment *"said out loud either way … an unpinned run that looks like a pinned one is the whole problem"*, and `git log -s` puts it in `b168490`, 2026-08-07 16:34 — fifteen days before the entry saying it does not exist. and the first is contradicted by the record. read out of git rather than re-run: the earlier artifact (`b26c2d4`, generated 2026-08-22t21:17:11z, 961 games / 95 diverged) carries `steering.team_store_pinned_to = "data\\\\team-pool-frozen"` and `steering.team_pool_teams = 8778`; the corrected one (`head`, 22:50:24z, 777 / 96) carries `"data/team-pool-frozen"` and the same 8778. `team_store` is the sole input to `swarm.buildswarm(..., { storedir })`, and `data/team-pool-frozen/` is a 2026-08-12 snapshot whose `games.bo3.jsonl` is 109,006,606 bytes against the live store's 167,972,026 — a live pool cannot yield the frozen pool's team count, so both runs read the frozen pool. what actually differs is `team_pool_picked` (1,968 against 1,597) and therefore `team_pool_digest` (`0d103fb9fa87` against `b2b61ec40281`), and `buildswarm` is asked for `max(games * 2, 18)` teams — i.e. the two runs requested different sample sizes. and the requested count is recoverable from the record, though neither artifact stores it. there is no `games_requested`, no argv and no flag block in either file — the same gap this row is about, one level up. but `buildswarm` computes `per = max(1, floor(max(games * 2, 18) / cfg.length))`, both runs carry 9 configs, and both publish `picked` per config: seven of the nine sit exactly on the cap, at 266 for `b26c2d4` and 213 for `head`. inverting that puts `--games` in [1197, 1201] for the earlier run and [959, 962] for the later one — so the two runs asked for materially different sizes, roughly 1200 against roughly 960, and 1200 and 960 are the only round numbers in those intervals. `coverage_stop` is `null` in both and the source says that field is *"null on a fixed-count run"*, so both took an explicit count and neither was `--until-covered`. the driver clamps, and it clamps per config rather than to the whole pool — the picker is `for (i = 0; i < matching.length && picked.length < per; i += step)`, and the record shows `omit-protect` at 99/99 and `omit-priority` at 7/7 in both runs. identical starvation is a third independent sign that the two read the same pool. so neither run got the count it asked for: about 1200 requested against 961 played (80.1%), and about 960 against 777 (80.9%). the shortfall is per-config starvation inside the frozen pool, present in both runs and in the same proportion — it is not a live store. what remains unknown and is not guessed: which exact integer was passed, and why the second run asked for the smaller one. nothing in the record carries a command line, and nothing was re-run to find out. neither figure is withdrawn by this row and neither may be entered in a retraction registry on its account: 11.69% is a rate on 777 games and 9.7% is a rate on 961, both on the frozen pool — two samples, not a pinned one and an unpinned one. what this row disputes is the cause that was published beside them, and nothing else. the real defect is that nothing reads the field. the only reader of `team_store_pinned_to` anywhere under `engine/` or `tests/` is `engine/replay_one.js:240`, and it reads the dump artifact rather than this one; no gate, no provenance clause and no `status.js` line compares a published claim's asserted pool against the artifact's declared pool or its `team_pool_digest`. a receipt nobody presents is not a receipt — which is the true form of what 5.74.0 was reaching for, and it is why a wrong pin would still be invisible today. #288 is the general row (a corpus snapshot id beside the release id in every artifact that reads a game file) and stays open; this is the specific case where the id already exists and is unread. what would decide it: a provenance clause that fails when a published rate names a pool the artifact does not declare, plus one re-measure of the 961/777 gap at a single requested game count. instrument owed: a provenance clause that fails when a published rate names a pool the artifact’s own `steering.team_store_pinned_to` and `team_pool_digest` do not declare.

open.title: THE DERIVED RETRACTION REGISTRY MATCHES ON A ROUNDED VALUE, SO ONE RETRACTED FIGURE ACCUSED 52 DOCUMENT LINES THAT SAY A
open.full: the derived retraction registry matches on a rounded value, so one retracted figure accused 52 document lines that say a different number — measured 2026-08-23 by measure, and it is live at baseline today. `retractionviolations` in `engine/docs_scan.js` accepts a hit when `number(e.value.tofixed(f.dp)) === f.value`. that tolerance was built for a real case — a document writing `63%` for a retracted `63.2%` is restating it — and it has no bound, so `(9.7).tofixed(0)` is `"10"` and a retracted `9.7%` matches every bare `10%` in the repository. measured: when one register row caused `9.7%` to enter the registry, that single entry produced 56 violations, of which 52 were a bare `10%` — a 93% false-positive rate on one entry, across `docs/engine.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/literature-v2.md`, `docs/miltank.md`, `docs/abra-whitepaper.md` and `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md`, hitting *"flare blitz's 10% burn"*, *"top 10% in singles"*, *"the 0-10% or 90-100% bin"* and *"~10% of its useful size"*. this is not about that one figure and it is not new — it is firing at baseline right now. with that entry removed the clause sits exactly at its baseline of 10 keys, and 12 of the 17 surviving raw violations are rounding collisions rather than exact matches: `docs/backlog.md:215` *"we produce the single most common set 48% of the time"* and `docs/archive/session-2026-08-02.md:113` *"sucker punch's 48% failure prices the missing opponent model"* are both accused of restating the retracted mirror figure 47.5%, and neither is about it. a second, independent half: `isdistinctive` admits any percent. it is `f => f.pct \|\| f.value >= 1000`, so a two-significant-figure percentage qualifies — and `docs/engine.md` carries the literal cell `\| into a bright powder holder (100 x 0.9 = 90) \| 10.3% \| 9.7% \|`, an accuracy, which any retracted `9.7%` rate would accuse forever. the registry's own header already makes this exact argument and then exempts percents from it: it records that a bare `17` once flagged ninety lines and concludes *"a registry that fires on every occurrence of a small integer is worse than no registry, because it is the thing people switch off."* a percent with two significant figures is a small integer wearing a unit. and the sharpest half: the extractor cannot tell a figure that is retracted from a figure named in a sentence about a retraction. rule 2 registers `<determiner> <number>` on any line containing `retract`, so a row whose finding is that a figure was not withdrawn is read as withdrawing it. that is what happened here: #367 states in terms that neither of its two rates is withdrawn, and the derivation entered one of them as retracted anyway. the row was reworded so it can only be read one way — which fixed the symptom and not this — and the baseline was deliberately not touched, because adding entries to `data/docs-currency-baseline.json` to quiet a false positive is the laundering that file's own rule forbids. this is #148 in a clause that is genuinely valuable when it fires correctly, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than loosening: the same derivation is what caught the deck's `63.2%` restated as fact after the white paper withdrew it in writing, and an over-firing gate is the one people learn to ignore. what would decide the fix is three cases and not a preferred implementation, because the shape decision is the open part: a retracted `63.2%` must still match a document writing `63%`; a retracted `9.7%` must not match a bare `10%`; a retracted `47.5%` must not match a sucker punch `48%` failure rate. the current rule satisfies only the first. instrument owed: a red demonstration pair per matching rule in `engine/docs_scan.js` on synthetic documents, in the style of the `equal`/`distinct` pairs the differential's own normaliser already carries, plus a distinctiveness floor for percents stated as a rule rather than as a magnitude

open.title: SHOWDOWN REFUSES A MOVE AND WE EXECUTE IT — 8 OF THE 47 NON-`event-missing` DIVERGENCES, EVERY MEMBER BOARD-MATERIAL, TH
open.full:
showdown refuses a move and we execute it — 8 of the 47 non-`event-missing` divergences, every member board-material, three sub-causes on one signature. filed 2026-08-23 by measure. read, never re-run, off `git show head:data/game-differential.json` (commit `192d917`): release `c66976713feb`, showdown `20ad99ffc9a5`, census pin `80e648f34d56`, team store pinned to `data/team-pool-frozen` (8,778 teams, 1,968 picked), 961 games / 95 diverged / 0 threw, generated 2026-08-23t02:40:37z. triage: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-remaining-56.md` (`ea26208`). the signature: the authority writes `\|-fail\|slot` and we write the move's effect, and in both sampled cases the authority's `\|move\|` line carries `\|\|[still]`. that pair — `this.battle.add('-fail', pokemon); this.battle.attrlastmove('[still]');` — is at `sim/battle-actions.ts:594-596`, the branch where `singleevent('try') && singleevent('preparehit') && runevent('preparehit')` returned an explicit `false`, and again at `:645-647` for an all-false `tryhit`, so the family narrows to those two gates without naming one of them. filed as one row with its sub-causes named, not as three rows: one signature, one place in the resolution order, and three rows would put three register entries on one fix.

(a) a stalling move that is not a shield never reaches the stall gate — 2 of 8, confirmed and source-cited. `unrelated event mismatch :: \|-fail\|p1b <> \|-singleturn\|p1b\|endure` and the same shape on `p2a`. `data/moves.ts:4816-4818` — `endure.onpreparehit(pokemon) { return !!this.queue.willact() && this.runevent('stallmove', pokemon); }` — is byte-identical to `protect`'s at `:13974-13976`; champions overrides `protect` (pp 5, `data/mods/champions/moves.ts:755`) and does not override `endure` at all. ours gates on the chooser's action kind rather than on the move being a stalling move — `it.a.kind==='protect'` — and `protectmoves` holds protect, detect, spikyshield, kingsshield, banefulbunker, burningbulwark, silktrap and maxguard, with endure absent from it, so both the `willact()` scan and the stall counter are skipped. *(both engine sites were verified at `engine/medicham2-browser.js:14901` and `:3891` by the coordinator on 2026-08-23 and are deliberately not re-read in this row: that file is under active engine edit tonight, so grep the symbols `protectmoves` and `_shieldpending`, never these line numbers.)* #232 closed on a family of six sharing one counter — endure among them — and five of the six reach the gate; #178 removed endure from `shieldsuser` for the right reason (it blocks nothing) and this gate is keyed on the same road. a fix for (a) is sitting uncommitted and unmeasured in the working tree from an agent that was stopped mid-task, so this sub-cause is not untouched — and nothing has yet measured whether that edit closes it or moves the divergence elsewhere.

(b) a trapping move re-applied to an already-trapped body — 2 of 8, mechanism confirmed from the format, instance a hypothesis. `\|-fail\|p2a <> \|-activate\|p1a\|trapped` and `\|-fail\|p1b <> \|-activate\|p2a\|trapped`. `meanlook` and `block` are both `onhit(target, source, move) { return target.addvolatile("trapped", source, move, "trapper"); }`, and `addvolatile` returns false on a repeat, so the second use fails; the `trapped` condition's `onstart(target) { this.add("-activate", target, "trapped"); }` is exactly the line we emit, so our announcement is right and the refusal is what is missing. this engine implements the repeat refusal per volatile (`applyattract`'s own comment: *"addvolatile refuses a repeat: no onrestart"*), never globally. a coverage-seeking driver re-clicks, which is why it surfaces here at all.

(c) four refusals that cannot be attributed at all — 4 of 8, unattributable by construction rather than unknown-cause. `\|-fail\|p2b <> \|-supereffective\|p1b\|1`, `\|-fail\|p2a <> \|-resisted\|p1a\|1`, `\|-fail\|p1a <> \|-damage\|p2a\|0 fnt`, `\|-fail\|p2b <> \|-damage\|p1a\|h/h`. all four carry `mentions: []` and `max_uses: undefined`, and none is among the 60 sampled `first_divergences`, so the file holds no species, no move and no preceding context for any of them. two damage a body the authority never damaged, one of those to a faint. the reason is the instrument's dump cap, filed as #375 — these do not become workable by thinking harder about them, and calling them unknown-cause would misname whose problem they are. what would decide (a) and (b): two bodies, one switches and the other clicks endure with nothing move-like left in the queue — assert `-fail` and no `-singleturn`, then endure on consecutive turns and assert the stall roll is consumed; and mean look twice into the same body — assert the second is `-fail` with no second `-activate`, with the same two clicks separated by a switch-out as the control that must succeed. endure is 5 corpus clicks; the fix is the keying, not the move.

open.full: 'good enough' is a usage-weighted threshold, not a row count — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. will, 2026-08-10: *'we do have to ask ourelves at what point is the engine good enough and has enough used features that it can perform its end goal'*. measured against the corpus rather than argued: 553,910 total move clicks; 781 (0.14%) land on a move that resolves to a whole no-op turn; 3,888 (0.70%) land on a move the roster says disagrees with the authority; the union is 4,208 = 0.76%. so 99.24% of real clicks land on a move with no known defect, and the game differential is 150/150 clean on real replayed games. the gate is a coverage standard and has been read as a sufficiency standard. its 45 open move rows are deliberately-staged edge cases, which is precisely why they survived — they barely occur. the honest test of sufficiency is roadmap #68: scale the differential from 150 games to 1,000+ real stored games. if it stays clean there, the remaining rows are polish and can run beside search work rather than blocking it, and the #99 quarantine can lift on a measured condition instead of a feeling. note the standing counter-evidence, which cuts the same way: `docs/measure.md` §0 carries a tight null at n=8,883 on the hypothesis that correctness fixes move the leaf at all

open.title: THE OPTIMIZATION PASS — hand MEDICHAM to Fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch
open.full: the optimization pass — hand medicham to fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch cannot fake. will, 2026-08-10: *'once we think medicham is good enough i plan to run some optimization programs to speed it up'* / *'handing it over to feeble 5 and saying make this go faster'*. dispatchable directly — the model is selectable per agent. the hazard is that 'faster' and 'different' are indistinguishable to a benchmark. an optimizer that shaves 30% by skipping a branch produces a beautiful number and a broken engine, and every existing test can still pass because those tests cover mechanics the branch never touches. so the pass runs three instruments, not one: `tests/bench-medicham.js` for the score (built 2026-08-10, pinned fixture, best-of-5, refuses to record a baseline under load — first reading 0.4341 ms/turn); the 500-move x 4-turn whole-board digest sweep for the verdict (2,000 cells; wire 147 used it to show only 11 moved, and that is the shape every optimization must reproduce at zero); and `tests/test-damage-stages.js` at 1728/1728 exact so arithmetic shortcuts cannot drift. sequencing, which decides how much work this is: the classifier cascade is both the most likely optimization target and the thing the remaining ~20 wires append to. restructure it first and the queued fixes land in the restructured version; do the wires first and the optimizer rewrites code that was just written

open.title: THE COST OF A FEATURE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHICH PATH IT SITS IN, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10.
open.full: the cost of a feature depends entirely on which path it sits in, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10. will: *'how many of these features will slow down the engine? cause if it costs nothing to have harvest in there, then sure we can, but if there is a time cost to it then maybe we otta reconsider'* — the right question, and the answer splits cleanly. hot path — runs on every click of every rollout: the damage chain and the ~40-branch classifier cascade. tonight's five wires cost +6.2% (0.776 -> 0.825 ms/turn, interleaved a/b across frozen releases under load), and the per-hit damage loop is almost certainly all of it, being the only wire that touched damage. cold path — fires once per turn on a trigger, and is effectively free: harvest, cud chew, cheek pouch, quick guard, the heal family. so harvest specifically: yes, free. the thing to actually guard is compounding — 6% per five wires, twenty more wires, and the engine is ~25% slower to serve 0.76% of clicks. that trade stops being worth it well before the queue empties, which is the argument for #76's ratchet firing on every wire rather than at the end

open.title: A FEW MILLION SELF-PLAY GAMES TO PROVE THE SAMPLER FIRES AT THE RATE WE DECLARED — Will's idea, and the right tool for t
open.full: a few million self-play games to prove the sampler fires at the rate we declared — will's idea, and the right tool for the question it actually answers. *'once we feel our engine is good we can have it play a few million games and then determine if our rate for accuracy and secondary effects is right'*, then, on the distinction: *'correct run the million games after we determine'*. so: #132 first (is the declared number right — free, exact), then this (does the code fire at it — statistical). this catches the failure a probe structurally cannot: a probe forces the outcome to test the mechanic, so a secondary declared at 30% that a bug makes fire at 0% or 100% passes every probe and every roster row. that is claude.md's founding failure — a capability absent while everything reports success — in the one place the existing instruments are blind. cost is not a constraint: at the measured 0.4341 ms/turn and a mean 3.6-turn rollout, a million games is roughly half an hour. compare observed firing rates against the declared chances with a confidence interval per move, and expect the answer to be boring — the value is the one that is not

open.full: position against three comparables, because the field is not empty and none of them is playing our game. vgc-bench (aamas 2026) — whose archive we already consume, and dropped from the fit for staleness (four days, mid-june, seven weeks old); `engine/corpus_shift.js` exists to measure the metagame distance and has never written an artifact. future sight ai — closed-source showdown bot, reportedly top 5% of the most popular format, matches revealed attributes to the most common set, ships a win-probability browser extension; also settles a naming question, since "future sight" is taken and this project names everything after pokémon. the pokeagent challenge (arxiv 2603.15563, neurips 2025, 100+ teams, two tracks) — by far the strongest reference of the three and not yet read. add sarantinos (arxiv 2212.13338, cambridge) as the closest published method: gen 7 random battles singles, peaked 33rd in the world, regret-minimisation opponent prediction, fills unknown properties from usage statistics, and explicitly rejects monte carlo sampling as too sample-inefficient — which is what miltank's leaf does. it also names our #29 independently: its first "biggest challenge" is keeping the team balanced, with a worked example that is the sack, and it asserts *"an ai agent cannot achieve this just by looking ahead with minmax or monte carlo tree search."* finally, its elo caveat is load-bearing for will's stated goal: comparing human and ai ratings is invalid unless they played each other — laddering with alakazam is exactly that, so the plan is sound and should say why
